chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Wilton Crawley's clarinet act and the TOBA circuit
summary: Crawley took his clarinet apart on stage and played upside down, toured the TOBA circuit, and Holmes now admires his tone.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, did Wilton Crawley do any of his stunts while in the studio?

Not while he's recording. Who's gonna see it? Nobody but us, and we didn't want to see it. Throwin' his clarinet and slap-tonguing on his clarinet and one-thing-and-another. He was quite good on that clarinet. I was actually surprised.
Well, the records to me show he had a lot of drive.

Yeah, that's what I say. He was very good. And I liked him now that I've heard him...you know, now, than I did then when I was recording with him. I couldn't stand him then. Well, I mean, i don't want to say I couldn't stand him. It was just a date, just another date, you know. But now that I can sit back and listen to the records, and... I mean he amazes me now. His tone is beautiful on them. I mean, for an...he's what you would call an unrehearsed musician. He just picks up the clarinet and starts doing funny things with it, and gets a wonderful
tone for...
Now, when he did his show, he was like a solo performer.

He was a solo performer. He'd come out and do his act. He had an act. And he'd come out there, and he'd take the clarinet all apart until he was playing nothing but... He'd take the bell off first, and he's playing the clarinet, then he'd take off the first joint, and then he'd take off the second joint, and then he'd take off the tuning barrel -- until he's left with nothing but the mouthpiece, and he's blowin' that. Then he comes back on the stage with the clarinet put back together again, he comes up and he's blowin', blowin'-blowin'-blowin', and he goes into some gymnastic turn or something, and the first thing you know, he's blowin' the clarinet and he's standin' on his head. His head is on the floor and he's still blowin' the clarinet.
You saw his show at the Lafayette?
Oh yeah. Many a time. Sure.
He was a popular performer.
He did all right. Oh yeah. He was very good. Very good with the clarinet.
I guess he traveled, then. He came in and out of New York?

Oh, yeah, he was... It was like he played what they called the TOBA circuit. I think there was about forty-some theatres in this circuit. They worked something like forty-some weeks out the year, from one town to another, all over the country.
So actually, he wasn't living here.
I don't know where he lived.
In other words, he sort of came into town, and...
Well, you know how everybody comes into New York. But I mean, he didn't live here.
No.
But he was a hell of a performer, and a hell of an act, anyway. But he was a little flaky up at the top.
